response:
The FTR (fiduciary termination right) is Section 9.1(d)(ii), which permits termination to enter into a Superior Company Proposal. The limitations on its exercise are set out in Section 7.3(e): the Company Acquisition Proposal must be unsolicited after the date of the Agreement and must not result from a **material breach of Section 7.3** (the no-shop provision), and it must constitute a Superior Company Proposal. There is no requirement regarding breach of other provisions of the agreement as a limitation on the FTR itself.

The precise language: "in the case of a Company Acquisition Proposal that was unsolicited after the date of this Agreement and that did not result from a material breach of this Section 7.3, terminate this Agreement pursuant to Section 9.1(d)(ii)..."

This matches choice A: "Material breach of no-shop resulting in a Superior Offer."
